articles.title: Sean 'Diddy' Combs moves from New Jersey prison to facility in Pennsylvania
articles.text:
Sean "Diddy" Combs has been transferred from a New Jersey correctional facility to a prison in Pennsylvania, the US Federal Bureau of Prisons says.

The rap mogul was moved to FCI Allenwood Low on Friday, a prison official said, but declined to discuss why he was moved, citing privacy, safety, and security reasons.

"His transfer from one low-security facility to another is an important distinction," Combs' spokesman told the BBC, adding that the move "is consistent with a decision made with safety and security in mind".

Combs, 56, who was sentenced to 50 months behind bars, has asked an appeals court to release him from prison and overturn his conviction on two prostitution-related crimes.

Combs' spokesman, Juda S Engelmayer, did not comment on an Associated Press report, external that Combs had been living a "luxury lifestyle" behind bars in New Jersey or on reports swirling about his health and treatment in lockup.

The move comes about two weeks after NBC News, external reported that the Bad Boy Records co-founder had access to mobile phones, liquor and other contraband at Fort Dix, as well as allegations that he had paid inmates to cook, clean and make his bed for him, and give him massages. He was also involved in two fights, according to NBC.

"It's because of the disruptive behaviour," Jose Rojas, union secretary for local federal prison employees, told NBC News of the move. "He's been causing too much trouble over there."

NBC reported Combs was stripped of 41 days for good conduct, pushing back his scheduled release date, which is now listed in the prison's online records as 2 March 2028. He was originally expected to be released in January 2028.

Engelmayer said he appreciates that the Federal Bureau of Prisons is "taking the safety and security of Sean and everyone involved seriously" and "we are grateful for the attention being given to his well-being and hope he can continue serving his time without unnecessary disruption".

The Federal Bureau of Prisons declined to comment on the reports.

"For privacy, safety, and security reasons, we do not comment on the conditions of confinement for any incarcerated individual, including whether a particular individual is the subject of allegations, investigations, or disciplinary sanctions," spokesman Donald Murphy said.

FCI Allenwood Low is a low-security federal correctional institution for male offenders that is about 155 miles (250 km) west of New York City.

The facility houses about 1,044 inmates, according to its website, a significantly smaller population than the one at Combs' previous facility, Fort Dix, of more than 4,200 inmates across two campuses. Allenwood also has medium and maximum security facilities nearby.

articles.title: Dame Judi Dench joins call to keep Archers in Birmingham
articles.text:
More than 100 current and former cast and crew members of The Archers, including Dame Judi Dench, have called on the BBC to keep the programme in Birmingham.

The appeal follows a decision to shelve plans for a dedicated studio at the broadcaster's new Digbeth headquarters.

Supporters say recording the drama elsewhere could affect its quality and future.

The BBC says the move is part of wider cost-saving measures and alternative options are being explored.

In a letter to director general Matt Brittin, actors, writers, directors and sound engineers argued that moving recordings away from the Midlands would have a "tangible impact" on the programme.

The letter compares the prospect to "Coronation Street leaving the north-west, or EastEnders leaving the south-east", adding that it risks "ripping out the heart of Ambridge".

Signatories said Birmingham had been central to the show's identity since it began and warned that separating cast and production teams could affect the way the programme is made.

"A flagship show deserves flagship facilities, from which both the BBC and the city of Birmingham would benefit for decades," the letter said.

It was signed by more than 100 current and former cast and crew members, including Dench, Felicity Jones and Kellie Bright, as well as representatives from Equity and the Writers' Guild.

The Archers, set in the fictional West Midlands village of Ambridge, celebrated its 75th anniversary earlier this year and has always been recorded in Birmingham.

The intervention follows the BBC's announcement that plans for a bespoke studio at its new Tea Factory headquarters in Digbeth would not go ahead.

The Worcestershire village of Inkberrow is believed to have inspired the show's fictional village of Ambridge, while The Old Bull Inn is closely associated with the show's pub, The Bull.

articles.title: London suburban housing project wins top UK architecture award
articles.text:
A suburban housing development in south London has won the UK's most prestigious architecture award, with judges praising its sensitive design and integration into the surrounding landscape.

Lion Green Road in Coulsdon, comprising 157 homes across five distinctive 13-sided blocks, was named winner of the 2026 Stirling Prize by the Royal Institute of British Architects (Riba).

Designed by Mary Duggan Architects and built with RUFF Architects, it combines affordable and private housing for Croydon Council.

Replacing a former car park on a challenging, sloping site that varies in height by eight metres (26ft), Riba president Chris Williamson praised the design as a "new approach to higher density development" creating "a new connection between the bustling Lion Green Road and a distinctive area of green parkland beyond".

Williamson told the BBC that until he went to study architecture he lived in a council estate in the East Midlands, "and every time I go back there all the council houses have been sold off, they're in private hands.

"Which in a way can be a good thing - we're in a homeowning democracy - but the sad thing is they haven't been replaced.

"Every time I go back - without getting too emotional - I think 'where would we have lived?'

"So to me that's why this particular project was important. I think a lot of people from that sort of background live in terrible accommodation - temporary accommodation which isn't safe or secure.

"These houses are fantastic and they're part of a mixed scheme so it's got a fantastic feel to it.

"For me it was a very inspirational, emotional, part of the process."

Duggan, who was brought up in south-west London, said the scheme "challenged conventional suburban housing layouts centred on roads, private gardens and clearly defined front and back spaces".

Winding paths and planting weave between the blocks, connecting them and linking shared outdoor spaces.

She said she wanted it to be a public space people felt they could belong to.

"Housing needs to be progressive. People who live in the building have access to green space, allotments."

The site fronts on to Lion Green Road, with low-rise green belt housing set on higher ground to the south and traditional suburban streets to the north.

The project was funded by Croydon Council as a public asset, and a change in building regulations meant it "fought against five or six circumstantial elements beyond the normal challenges".

The building was praised by the jury for its "inventive and site-specific response to a highly constrained plot".

Buildings are assessed across a range of criteria, including design vision, innovation, sustainability, functionality, and the ability to delight users and visitors.

articles.title: Off Campus star collaboration 'gave me chills', says Babydoll singer
articles.text:
The singer behind the TikTok viral hit Babydoll says collaborating with an Off Campus star was "mind-boggling".

Jamie Miller, who is originally from Pontprennau in Cardiff, was close to calling it quits on his music career at the start of 2026, deciding it was his "last chance", financially and emotionally.

But over the summer everything changed when Babydoll caught the attention of people on social media, leading to a viral dance, his first UK top 10 single, and reaching number one in the US iTunes pop chart.

When Miller saw a comment from actor Antonio Cipriano, saying he "needed this song", he sent him a message suggesting he feature on a recording – then "panicked" and added "haha, joking".

"I'm a fan of Antonio's voice, and I have been a fan for a long time," he said.

"He messaged back and was like, 'If you're actually not joking, I'd be honoured'."

Cipriano headed to Los Angeles, where Miller now lives, and they recorded Babydoll on the day they first met, external.

"It was the best time ever," said Miller.

"We're coming up at the same time, he has an amazing career in acting and I feel like the stars aligned even for us to do this and the world is rallying around us as a duo too. The opportunities that we're having right now are incredible."

Amazon Prime Video's ice hockey romance series Off Campus – based on a book series by Elle Kennedy - has similarly taken the world by storm this year, ranking as the third most-watched series launch in the platform's history, external.

It has raised the profile of numerous artists, with a soundtrack merging old favourites with new music.

Asked if he would like to be involved with the series in future, Miller said: "I'm such a fan of the show. I think it's absolutely incredible what they're doing, what Antonio is doing. In any capacity, I would love to. We'll see."

On Friday, the original version of Babydoll moved from number three to number two in the official UK charts - beaten only by Taylor Swift's Patient Zero.

Cipriano told BBC Wales Miller was "one of the best vocalists I've ever heard", adding he had been a fan of Miller's voice "for years".

He described becoming "instant best friends" on their first meeting because they're "very similar... like a twin flame situation".

"Especially in the music industry, I'm new to it but I know and have heard that it's not necessarily always the easiest thing to find genuine connections and relationships in this field, and it feels as genuine as it can get. I love him."

He added Miller's music was a "breath of fresh air".

"It's making people dance again... [let's] get it to number one in the UK baby."

Miller also recently supported The Jonas Brothers on the US leg of their tour, and said bringing Cipriano out as a guest star at some of the shows was "mind-boggling".

"I think the easiest thing about it was we're doing it together, for the first time. It was his first arena, it was my first arena, and I think that's the most amazing situation to be in, because we can lean on each other.

"Backstage we would say to each other, 'we're so lucky, our lives are not normal, we're going out to play for 20,000 people, what are we doing bro?'.

"Introducing him gave me chills because, as well as my dreams coming true right now, his dreams are too.

"It's so nice and needed, to have a friend who can guide you through."

Asked about the possibility of Miller joining him on Off Campus, Cipriano said: "That would be awesome. Like, if he came on as the musical guest and then Logan just randomly got up there and sang with him - that's cool."

At 19, Miller competed in The Voice UK, coming third place with coach Jennifer Hudson.

But his love for music first began accidentally, when he took part in a primary school show.

"If you auditioned for the play, then you got to skip out math class," he recalled.

"Just to see the reaction from the teachers after they asked me to sing a song, was just absolutely like 'I want to do this, this is actually incredible.'

"All my mates were rugby players and football players, whereas I just wanted to do music. After that one audition, I was hooked."

Now 29, Miller admits the past couple of years have been "really tough", adding changes in the music industry and in his personal life had left him feeling quite lost.

"Going into this year was my last chance to try and cut through. This industry is really hard, it's really expensive as well," he said.

"I think the thing with success, people think you have a lot of money... I didn't really see that side of that. So financially, this year, I couldn't really make it work anymore. I was on my last legs."

Miller said he "never had any social media campaign" planned and it "happened the most organic way possible".

As the Babydoll dance took hold of social media, Miller collaborated with an array of stars including actors Jennifer Love Hewitt, Lucy Hale and Julianne Hough, as well as popstar Meghan Trainor.

"All these incredible people I've been able to do it with, they've said it themselves, they've said 'we needed this song'.

"From all sides of the world, it's kind of unified people in a way, and it's just a beautiful thing to be a part of something that made someone smile."

Miller said he was "proud" of his new music and was excited to share his latest album with the world and to tour it – in particular, he said, to bring it to Wales.

Cipriano added he had never been to Wales but it "looked like a beautiful place" and he "would absolutely love to", in particular to meet Miller's family, with whom he had "instantly hit it off".

Miller said the non-stop nature of the past couple of months had been "really hard to process".

"It feels like so many life changes are happening around me, but I'm still the same person. It's dystopian, in a way.

"Especially being from Wales, you don't really see stuff like this happening to people all the time. Tom Jones is absolutely incredible, but I feel like he's really been the one that's flown the flag, and rightfully so.

"I'm very appreciative for everything that's going on right now, and thank my lucky stars. I just hope I'm doing Wales proud, to be honest."
